text:
Direct evidence for title-similarity negatives in BERT4Rec without pretrained embeddings is limited in the sources found. [GenNi](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.03645) supports informative negatives in sequential recommendation, but defines difficulty using the current model’s user–item preferences, not title overlap. Adjacent evidence: [DPR](https://aclanthology.org/2020.emnlp-main.550.pdf) improves retrieval by adding one BM25-selected negative to in-batch negatives; adding two provides no further benefit. BM25 mining requires no pretrained embeddings, although DPR’s trained retriever does. This supports lexical confusability as a candidate-mining hypothesis, not an established BERT4Rec result.

False-negative safeguards matter. [SimANS](https://aclanthology.org/2022.emnlp-industry.56.pdf) finds negatives near positive relevance scores more useful and less risky than the highest-scoring negatives; its bands concern learned relevance scores, not lexical cosine thresholds. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) independently documents false negatives in sequential recommendation. Neither establishes transferable title-similarity bands, random/lexical mixture weights, or missing-title policies.

A reproducible experiment could therefore use fixed title normalization and corpus-fitted TF–IDF cosine or token Jaccard, deterministic similarity-rank bands and item-ID tie-breaking. Treat these as proposed safeguards: mix a modest lexical fraction with uniform negatives; report sampling probability separately from loss weighting; exclude the target and observed training-history positives; reject near-duplicate titles; fall back to uniform sampling for missing text or empty pools. Fix preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42. Compare against uniform-only sampling with identical negative counts and loss, selecting bands and mixture weights using validation only. Measure lexical overlap and model scores separately: lexical similarity does not establish model-score hardness or true irrelevance.
